sampling_model.design: Large-\(N\), fixed-\(T\) observational panel with a predeclared stopped-Hankel chart, polynomial frame, and cohort-time grid.
sampling_model.units: The panels \(W_i\) are independent draws from \(P_W\); within-panel dependence is generated by the untreated hidden Markov law and staggered adoption.
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and occurs with a current-hidden-state hazard before the period's untreated outcome, with fresh adoption randomization conditionally independent of future untreated innovations.
sampling_model.overlap: State hazards are interior and every target cohort has mass bounded away from zero on the inference stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All nuisance objects are finite stopped-word moments evaluated through one ordered Hankel minor fixed before outcomes and one fixed coefficient-normalized polynomial frame; no empirical latent labeling, rank-revealing minor selection, or adaptive frame search is used. The estimator is a total Borel map with sequential half-gap and uncovered-inverse gates and fixed fallback outputs. The Kim--Lee usability screen jointly bootstraps the same moment vector and applies only preregistered rank, gap, residual, cohort-mass, and ATT-half-width thresholds.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states under A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\) and A2 ergodicity with a strictly positive stationary law, and characterizes its non-permutation equivalence.
Theorem 1 identifies ATT from repeated measurements, while Section 3.3 states that evolving hidden shocks create a staggered-selection failure for that construction.
Theorem 1 identifies group-time ATT under conditional parallel trends and the paper establishes simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap inference.

Under an interactive fixed-effects law for untreated outcomes and adoption-group moment and rank conditions, the main identification theorem recovers group-time ATT from observed cohort moments, with joint asymptotic inference developed in Proposition 1 and the multiplier-bootstrap corollary.
Theorem 6 bounds HMM prediction error under observable singular-value separation.
Proposition 1 represents the spectral HMM estimator as an equivalent moment estimator, and Section 3.4 optimizes its moment weighting.

The paper estimates effects of a dynamic treatment on potential latent-state distributions by inverse-probability-weighted hidden-Markov maximum likelihood under observed-confounder treatment assignment assumptions.

The paper combines a bias-adjusted three-step latent Markov measurement model with a parametric g-formula under exchangeability, positivity, consistency, no interference, and latent-Markov restrictions.
The paper identifies staggered-adoption effects by design-based matching on observed histories under its stated identifying conditions and applies the method to six-period Netflix--IPTV data.
The paper develops estimation and inference across weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences.

body.tldr: State-dependent adoption generally defeats observed-history parallel-trends comparisons because missing future untreated outcomes are selected by latent state. A finite stopped-panel law nevertheless identifies every adopter cohort's untreated path law when adoption hazards are constant within current-emission alias classes. Predictive rank gives chart-independent minimal coordinates, while computation and inference use a preregistered Hankel chart. On a fixed emission-partition stratum, unequal within-alias hazards and one-step forecasts generate a continuum of same-observed-law realizations with different ATT. The exact positive witness has ATT gap \(2/185\). More strongly, the two-parameter family \(\mathfrak C(\eta,\zeta)\) has one-panel divergence \(O(\zeta^2)\) while its target gap is first order in \(\eta\); fixed positive \(\eta\) and \(N\zeta_N^2\to0\) rule out uniform consistency and uniformly honest shrinking bands over the full unseparated neighborhood. The \(N^{-1/4}\) statement is a local corollary. The exceptional binary three-state legal-lift frontier is genuinely bivariate and remains open, as does the Kim--Lee empirical certificate.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD and interactive-fixed-effects methods use observed histories or adoption-cohort moments, while causal latent-Markov procedures impose their own recovery and ignorability structures. Weiss and Nadler are an algebraic ancestor, not a containing model: they study an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states under A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\) and A2 ergodicity with a positive stationary law. This stopped two-terminal model permits arbitrary \(\alpha\), and its binary \(K=3\) instance cannot satisfy A1 because three binary probability mass functions lie in a two-dimensional function space. Neither class contains the other, so no Weiss--Nadler converse transfers. Existing spectral results also do not select a preregistered stopped-Hankel minor or identify cohort continuation from an adoption terminal.
project_justification.niche: The observable adoption terminal can identify a similarity-invariant hazard operator even when non-permutation latent realizations share the stopped law. The converse is stated only on a fixed emission-partition stopped-HMM stratum. Near the repeated-emission boundary, the independent hazard- and emission-splitting parameters expose both local weak separation and failure of any nontrivial uniform rate without a coupling restriction.
project_justification.fill: The project proves hazard-lift path-law invariance, a fixed-partition generic converse, and an exact \(2/185\) stress test; supplies a total guarded fixed-chart estimator with regular-subset simultaneous inference; and strengthens the collision analysis to the two-parameter family \(\mathfrak C(\eta,\zeta)\), including nonuniform-consistency and nonshrinking-band impossibility over the displayed unseparated neighborhood. It leaves the complete bivariate one-alias-block legal-lift frontier, with explicit invariants and component enumeration, as an open question, and separately leaves the Kim--Lee empirical certificate open.

body.related_work: Weiss and Nadler study an ordinary all-length stationary parametric-output HMM with exactly two aliased states, A1 output-family linear independence of order \(n\), and A2 ergodic transition with a strictly positive stationary law. Their similarity calculations are an algebraic ancestor of the legal-fiber construction, but their class neither contains nor is contained in this stopped two-terminal class: the latter allows arbitrary \(\alpha\), while three binary emission mass functions cannot meet their A1 linear-independence condition. Their connectedness and converse conclusions therefore are not imported. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish generic finite-window identification, while Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister use separation conditions that exclude exact repeated emissions. Bartolucci and Farcomeni give a killed-forward latent event-history model without the proposed causal invariant. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted hidden-Markov likelihood, and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside a parametric g-formula. The fixed-partition generic converse diagnoses transporting those workflows while additionally demanding continuation determined by the observed stopped law; their own structural assumptions are not contradicted, and hazard lifting does not identify their latent-state estimands. Callaway and Sant'Anna identify group-time ATT and simultaneous inference under conditional parallel trends. Callaway and Tsyawo use interactive fixed effects and adoption-date moments; their functional has neither a state-dependent stopping mark nor alias-fiber invariance, while hazard lifting does not impose their factor structure. Kim and Lee use observed-history matching in the six-period Netflix--IPTV panel, and Ishimaru uses repeated measurements outside evolving hidden selection. The exact pair and the two-parameter collision family are stress tests, not contradictions of those papers, because their identifying assumptions are not asserted on the displayed laws. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang provide ordinary-HMM observable operators, but predictive rank guarantees only that some minor is nonsingular. Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez provide a moment-estimation template but not the stopped-chart, de-killing, or frame conditions. Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent; the collision result is scoped to the displayed family and does not contradict any comparator theorem or separated regular domain. These sources are informed-by comparators, not results claimed to be strictly tightened.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Sampling noise destroys exact commutativity and repeated eigenvalues, so the estimator uses a fixed written-order polynomial dictionary and a least-squares off-model extension. Full stopped-Hankel rank ensures that some \(K\)-minor works, not that the ordered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\) fixed before outcomes does; all Euclidean separation claims use that chart and coefficient normalization. The total estimator applies inverse formulas only behind fixed half-gap gates and otherwise returns preregistered defaults. For the displayed collision family, both members are legal hazard-lift laws for all sufficiently small \(\eta,\zeta>0\), one-panel KL divergence is \(O(\zeta^2)\), and \(\sigma_3(V_D)=\Theta(\zeta)\), with coefficient \(6250/(17\sqrt{1266})\) as \(\eta\to0\). The counterfactual gap is \(63\eta/544+O(\eta^2+\zeta)\). Thus \(N\zeta_N^2\to0\) and \(\zeta_N=o(\eta_N)\) make the product laws merge while preserving either a first-order local gap or, for fixed small \(\eta_0>0\), a nonzero limiting gap. Without a coupling restriction between hazard and emission splitting, the full unseparated neighborhood has no nontrivial uniform rate. The legal-frontier region is bivariate; univariate sign methods require a proved reduction.
body.honest_scope: The point-identification theorem fixes the hidden order and finite alphabet, uses \(T\ge2K-1\), and assumes homogeneous untreated dynamics, invertible killed dynamics, positive cohort masses, and sequential hazard randomization. It identifies finite untreated cohort path laws, not latent labels, transitions, or initial probabilities. Predictive rank gives a chart-independent minimal realization and guarantees existence of some nonsingular minor; displayed formulas and inference additionally require the preregistered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\). The generic converse concerns future lags and is proved within a fixed emission-partition realization stratum of \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}\). The exact \(2/185\) witness and collision family concern only \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), and \(r=1\). The collision impossibility is over the displayed full unseparated hazard-lift neighborhood: it rules out uniform consistency and uniformly honest \(o(1)\)-diameter bands there, while making no claim against comparator methods on their own maintained domains. Fixed-gap compact regular subsets retain pointwise root-\(N\) inference. The open legal-lift classification is restricted to the positive interior binary three-state, six-date, one-alias-block stratum and now requires a complete bivariate component analysis; no connectedness is imported from Weiss--Nadler. The Kim--Lee data are unavailable, so no empirical certificate is claimed. Unknown order, continuous outcomes, approximate homogeneity, sharp tolerance bounds, adaptive chart selection, constrained-model efficiency, and finite-sample remainders remain open.
